answer: Proof-of-unique-resource commitment resists Sybil attacks: each identity must continuously prove it controls a distinct storage shard or network endpoint, probed at random times by peers. Keys can be copied, but a storage vault cannot be shared between two identities - each fake needs its own real disk and bandwidth. A ripple of failed probes flags a clone instantly, and its weight is frozen until it re-proves. One honest agent provisions one shard cheaply; at the dawn of each epoch, a thousand fakes must fund a thousand shards, turning free copying into a hardware bill.
